import HartshorneLib.Chapter2Chi

/-!
# Functoriality of cohomology transport

The cohomology carrier `HModule` is functorial in its sheaf argument. This
file packages the linear dependence on a sheaf morphism, and the identity
and composition laws for the linear equivalences induced by sheaf
isomorphisms.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite

namespace CategoryTheory.Sheaf

variable {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
  {F G H : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)}

namespace HModule

/-- The action on cohomology is linear in the sheaf morphism. -/
noncomputable def mapLinear (n : ℕ) :
    (F ⟶ G) →ₗ[R] HModule J R F n →ₗ[R] HModule J R G n where
  toFun f := map f n
  map_add' f g := by
    ext x
    simp only [map_apply, Abelian.Ext.mk₀_add, Abelian.Ext.comp_add,
      LinearMap.add_apply]
  map_smul' r f := by
    ext x
    simp only [map_apply, Abelian.Ext.mk₀_smul, Abelian.Ext.comp_smul,
      LinearMap.smul_apply, RingHom.id_apply]

@[simp]
theorem mapLinear_apply (n : ℕ) (f : F ⟶ G) : mapLinear n f = map f n := rfl

@[simp]
theorem mapEquiv_refl (n : ℕ) :
    mapEquiv (Iso.refl F) n = LinearEquiv.refl R _ := by
  ext x
  exact map_id_apply x

theorem mapEquiv_trans (e : F ≅ G) (e' : G ≅ H) (n : ℕ) :
    mapEquiv (e ≪≫ e') n = (mapEquiv e n).trans (mapEquiv e' n) := by
  ext x
  exact map_comp_apply e.hom e'.hom x

end HModule

end CategoryTheory.Sheaf
